text:
inc-bot: INCIDENT created: Customer Greenline (private VPC) — increased 502/504s from tenant pool behind NLB. Severity: P1. Pinged on-call rota.
eng-oncall-amit: got page, pulling alert details. seeing NLB target health flapping for tenant-subnet-a across two AZs.
sre-jordan: adding context — yesterday we rolled SG tighten for tenant network (PR #2781). Could be related. Flow logs show 502 responses from origin on port 8080.
eng-oncall-amit: @net-ops-lena can you confirm if SGs were applied to the NLB target instances or to the app ENIs? quick check: `aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids sg-0a1b2c3d`
net-ops-lena: checking now. I see the policy applied to app ENIs (sg-0a1b2c3d) and there is an explicit deny for `0.0.0.0/0` on ephemeral range 32768-65535 — that might block healthchecks from NLB targets.
prod-ops-ty: NLB health checks come from the NLB nodes, source ports vary. We should allow the ephemeral range from the VPC CIDR for target SGs, or pin the healthcheck by source.
eng-oncall-amit: can we test curl from a bastion into the app instance on the healthcheck path? `curl -v http://10.10.5.22:8080/health`
net-ops-lena: bastion -> app: connection refused intermittently. When connection works, app returns `200 {"ok":true}`. When it fails, tcp reset.
sre-jordan: logs from the app show `connection reset by peer` around the same timestamps as healthcheck fails. Could be OS-level conntrack exhaustion on the app host.
eng-oncall-amit: run `ss -s` and `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max` please.
net-ops-lena: nf_conntrack_max=65536, ss shows many TIME_WAIT and SYN_RECV. We also see NAT instance (tenant-proxy) CPU spike.
solutions-cs-rosa: customer-facing note: Greenline reports degraded feature X; receiving elevated error rates since 09:12 UTC. ETA for first update?
eng-oncall-amit: immediate mitigation: open SG to allow ephemeral ports from NLB health nodes to app ENIs and temporarily route traffic away from the most saturated nat host. Rolling config now. :wrench:
net-ops-lena: applied temporary SG rule: allow 10.10.0.0/16 ephemeral 32768-65535 -> sg-0a1b2c3d. Monitoring.
prod-ops-ty: routing one AZ out of service for the tenant: set NLB target weight 0 for targets in AZ-b to drain.
sre-jordan: also increasing nf_conntrack_max to 200k on the affected app hosts via sysctl as short-term. Applying to all in tenant-ASG.
eng-oncall-amit: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/vpc-private-nlb-healthcheck-triage — follow steps 2-5.
customer-tara: thanks — we see errors drop a bit. still some 502 spikes but MUCH improved. please keep me posted, our SREs are standing by.
solutions-cs-rosa: I told customer we have a mitigation and are doing config rollbacks if needed.
net-ops-lena: after SG change + conntrack increase, target health stabilized across AZs. 10m consecutive healthy checks.
sre-jordan: leaving longer-term action items: 1) revert SG tighten PR and move to a staged rule that allows NLB ephemeral sources; 2) add conntrack alert for tenant pools; 3) document pinning NLB source ranges for private deployments.
eng-oncall-amit: on-call handoff: I'm going to stay on for monitoring for another 30m then hand to @sre-jordan at 9154321500 UTC.
prod-ops-ty: creating incident postmortem ticket: INC-2026-0047, linking logs and runbook steps.
solutions-cs-rosa: customer update sent: "We've applied a temporary configuration to restore traffic and are investigating a permanent fix. We'll follow up with RCA." :email:
custome­r-tara: appreciate the quick response, please include timeline for permanent fix.
eng-oncall-amit: noted. final note: primary impact window ~09:12-09:25 UTC, mitigated by SG relaxation + conntrack bump + AZ drain. Leaving monitoring open.
inc-bot: INCIDENT update: status -> mitigated. next update scheduled in 30m or on any regression.
sre-jordan: moving to owner for RCA and follow-ups. Closing on-call active page.
net-ops-lena: will open PR to adjust SG rules with explicit NLB source ranges and add test plan.
solutions-cs-rosa: I'll coordinate customer follow-up and timeline.
eng-oncall-amit: handing off to @sre-jordan now. :handshake:
